title: Fourth moment bound by Fourier sparsity
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Write $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$ for its Fourier coefficient at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $s$ be the number of subsets $S$ for which $\widehat f(S)\ne0$. Then $\mathbb E_x[f(x)^4]\le s\bigl(\mathbb E_x[f(x)^2]\bigr)^2$, where the expectations are uniform over the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
